site.name: Cash Mine
site.location: Gold Hill Mining District, Boulder County
overview: Cash Mine is a historic gold-silver telluride mine in Boulder County's Gold Hill Mining District. The claim dates to 1872 and the mine developed into a substantial underground operation west of Boulder.
Historic mapping and later mining records document a deep shaft and multiple underground levels, while modern USGS-derived mapping preserves the mine locality near Gold Hill.

timeline.text: The Cash Mine claim was staked during the Gold Hill district's telluride-mining era.
A surviving Harrison S. Cobb mine map documented the Cash Mine shaft and underground levels and recorded the shaft at 746 feet.
Mines Magazine described the Cash as Colorado's only active underground gold mine at that time, reflecting the property's unusually long operating history.

moreHistory: The Cash Mine lies in the Gold Hill Mining District, one of Boulder County's earliest hard-rock mining areas. County programming and mining-history sources identify the property as a gold-silver telluride mine whose lode claim was staked in 1872.

The Carnegie Library for Local History preserves a 1961 underground map showing the Cash shaft and levels; the catalog record lists the shaft as 746 feet deep. This provides unusually specific documentation of the mine's underground development.

USGS Mineral Resources Data System-derived locality records identify the Gold Hill Cash Mine as a gold mine with silver also reported and provide a stable mine-level location near 40.06193, -105.40083.
